messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://www.mdpi.com/2072-666X/13/4/498/pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.3390/mi13040498

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Flexible & Transparent Digital Microfluidics Fabrication Protocol (Droplet Manipulation and Actuation Characterization on an ITO/PET/PE EWOD Device)

REAGENTS USED:
  - DI Water (droplet manipulation demo and contact-angle/leakage/driving-voltage characterization, 8-10 uL droplets)
  - 0.1 M Sodium Chloride Solution (contact-angle characterization, 10 uL droplets)
  - 1 M Sodium Chloride Solution (contact-angle characterization, 10 uL droplets)

STEPS:
1. Droplet Manipulation Demo: A DI water droplet is dispensed onto the transparent ITO/PET electrode array (2 mm x 2 mm electrodes, 0.5 mm spacing) and actuated by electrowetting to move straight and turn across the array.
2. Droplet Merging Demo: A second DI water droplet is dispensed and actuated to merge with the first droplet on the same electrode array.
3. Contact Angle Characterization: DI water, 0.1 M NaCl, and 1 M NaCl droplets (10 uL each) are individually dispensed and actuated under increasing AC voltage (1 kHz); the contact angle of each droplet is measured, decreasing nearly linearly with voltage before reaching saturation.
4. Leakage Current Characterization: A droplet is dispensed and held between two electrodes on the Rain-X-treated PE film and PET substrate; the AC voltage supply is swept from 250 Vrms to 450 Vrms in 25 V increments, with the leakage current density measured five times at each voltage step.
5. Minimum Driving Voltage Characterization: DI water droplets of 8, 10, and 12 uL are each dispensed and actuated with electrode on/off switching times of 1, 2, 3, and 4 s, and the minimum voltage required for reliable droplet movement is measured at each combination.

INTERPRETATION: Successful device performance is confirmed by reliable droplet dispensing, translocation, and merging on the thin (less than 200 um), flexible, and optically transparent ITO/PET/PE device; a water contact angle increase from 78.3 to 103.2 degrees after Rain-X treatment; leakage current densities that remain low (tens to ~190 nA/mm2) across the 250-450 Vrms operating range, confirming the PE film is an acceptable thin dielectric; contact angles for DI water and NaCl solutions that decrease with increasing voltage toward saturation; and minimum driving voltages that decrease with slower electrode on/off switching and increase with droplet volume, together validating the device as a low-cost, transparent alternative to conventional glass/silicon EWOD chips for colorimetric and optical droplet-based assays.

ir.content:
main:
	d11[0] = dispense(di_water)
bsbbr_2_h:
	PHI REPEAT_41 = {REPEAT_40,REPEAT_42}
	PHI d12 = {d11,d13}
	if REPEAT_41[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_3_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_4_f
bsbbr_3_t:
	d13[0] = mix(d12[0], d12[0]) @ 1.0SECOND
	REPEAT_42[0] = REPEAT_41[0] - 1
bsbbr_4_f:
	d21[0] = dispense(di_water)
	merged1[0] = mix(d12[0], d21[0]) @ 1.0SECOND
	dispose(merged1[0])
	water_drop1[0] = dispense(di_water)
	water_angle_reading1[0] = detect(fluorescence, water_drop1[0]) @ 1.0SECOND
	dispose(water_drop1[0])
	nacl_low_drop1[0] = dispense(nacl_0_1m)
	nacl_low_angle_reading1[0] = detect(fluorescence, nacl_low_drop1[0]) @ 1.0SECOND
	dispose(nacl_low_drop1[0])
	nacl_high_drop1[0] = dispense(nacl_1m)
	nacl_high_angle_reading1[0] = detect(fluorescence, nacl_high_drop1[0]) @ 1.0SECOND
	dispose(nacl_high_drop1[0])
	leak_drop1[0] = dispense(di_water)
bsbbr_5_h:
	PHI REPEAT_91 = {REPEAT_90,REPEAT_92}
	PHI leakage_reading1 = {leakage_reading0,leakage_reading2}
	PHI REPEAT_51 = {REPEAT_50,REPEAT_52}
	if REPEAT_91[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_6_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_10_f
bsbbr_6_t:
bsbbr_7_h:
	PHI leakage_reading2 = {leakage_reading1,leakage_reading3}
	PHI REPEAT_52 = {REPEAT_51,REPEAT_53}
	if REPEAT_52[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_8_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_9_f
bsbbr_8_t:
	leakage_reading3[0] = detect(fluorescence, leak_drop1[0]) @ 1.0SECOND
	REPEAT_53[0] = REPEAT_52[0] - 1
bsbbr_9_f:
	REPEAT_92[0] = REPEAT_91[0] - 1
bsbbr_10_f:
	dispose(leak_drop1[0])
bsbbr_11_h:
	PHI REPEAT_31 = {REPEAT_32,REPEAT_3}
	PHI min_voltage_reading1 = {min_voltage_reading2,min_voltage_reading}
	PHI vdrop1 = {vdrop3,vdrop}
	PHI REPEAT_43 = {REPEAT_44,REPEAT_4}
	if REPEAT_31[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_12_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_16_f
bsbbr_12_t:
	vdrop2[0] = dispense(di_water)
bsbbr_13_h:
	PHI min_voltage_reading2 = {min_voltage_reading1,min_voltage_reading3}
	PHI vdrop3 = {vdrop2,vdrop4}
	PHI REPEAT_44 = {REPEAT_43,REPEAT_45}
	if REPEAT_44[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_14_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_15_f
bsbbr_14_t:
	min_voltage_reading3[0] = detect(fluorescence, vdrop3[0]) @ 1.0SECOND
	vdrop4[0] = mix(vdrop3[0], vdrop3[0]) @ 1.0SECOND
	REPEAT_45[0] = REPEAT_44[0] - 1
bsbbr_15_f:
	dispose(vdrop3[0])
	REPEAT_32[0] = REPEAT_31[0] - 1
bsbbr_16_f:
	NOP

numeric_mismatches.field: fabrication steps (laser ablation, PE lamination, Rain-X treatment) not modeled
numeric_mismatches.note: These are substrate/electrode manufacturing steps performed once during device construction, not droplet-level chip operations; BioScript has no primitive for laser patterning, film lamination, or surface-treatment chemistry, so only the post-fabrication droplet experiments are translated.

numeric_mismatches.field: AC voltage magnitude and frequency not encoded
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper's actuation voltage (0-500 Vrms, 1 kHz sinusoidal signal via function generator and high-voltage amplifier) and all specific voltage values (250-450 Vrms leakage sweep, per-condition minimum driving voltages in Figure 9b) have no corresponding BioScript field; only the loop/repeat counts approximating the number of test conditions are encoded.

numeric_mismatches.field: detect fluorescence used as stand-in for contact angle / leakage current / driving voltage readouts
numeric_mismatches.note: None of these measurements are fluorescence-based in the paper (contact angle is measured optically via microscope image analysis; leakage current via ammeter; driving voltage via visual confirmation of droplet motion); 'detect fluorescence' is used only because it is the sole detect module exposed by BioScript's grammar, standing in for a generic instrumented readout.

numeric_mismatches.field: droplet volumes 8, 10, 12 uL and electrode on/off times 1-4s
numeric_mismatches.note: The Figure 9b test matrix (3 droplet volumes x 4 switching times = 12 conditions) is approximated with a repeat 3 x repeat 4 nested loop structure, but the literal volume (uL) and timing (s) values from the figure are not attached to the dispense/detect operations beyond the fixed 8 units per droplet.
